tools.name: api_guide
tools.description: Return the pre-written agent guide for building a Bosatsu API with checked access rules. Call this first. Deterministic documentation; no model-generated advice. With no arguments it returns every section; with section it returns the sections whose title contains that text (case-insensitive) and, on no match, the list of titles.

section.description: Optional title, or part of one: only the matching sections are returned. Omit for the whole guide.

tools.name: api_scaffold
tools.description: Generate a Yichus-first Bosatsu API module: structs, Yichus/Access rules, owner-scoped or public handlers, and a Yichus/Service routing table, plus a matching Yichus/Frontend::FrontendSpec (frontendSource) for api_frontend. The result compiles and verifies; edit it, then api_verify.

package_name.description: Bosatsu package, PascalCase segments separated by slashes, e.g. My/Notes/Api

resources.description: JSON array of {name, fields:[{name,type}], policy}. type is String, Int, or Bool. policy is owner or public.

tools.name: api_add_rule
tools.description: Return a one-line Yichus/Access AccessRule snippet to paste into an existing AccessSpec list.

resource.description: Table name as passed to Yichus/Data::table, e.g. notes

tools.name: api_verify
tools.description: Rerun the available safety checks from the typed IR of the given Bosatsu sources. Reports which properties still hold after edits. Topology is an input: undeclared defaults to multi-instance, where RMW and interleaving findings are violations. When the sources declare a Yichus/Organize AbstractionSpec or GroupSpec, the declared-structure property checks every declared claim the way api_organize's abstractions and layers lenses do: proven when all converge, violated when any declared claim diverges (a generator that does not hold its declared guard responsibility, a member that does not use its generator, or a package that uses a group its GroupSpec does not allow; the claim is named with its location), blocked when a declared generator, member, concept or package is absent or the declarations cannot be evaluated, and a warning when a GroupSpec allows a use the code never makes. Sources with no such declaration get no declared-structure property. Warnings do not make proven false unless block_on_warnings lists them. Do not deploy unless proven is true.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files for the API module.

instances.description: Deployment topology: 1 for a single engine instance, many (default) for multiple instances sharing one DB.

block_on_warnings.description: Optional JSON array of property ids (for example ["rmw-transactions", "integrity"]) or ["all"]. An id must name a property this verdict has; declared-structure exists only when the sources declare a spec; use all to block every warning whatever the program declares. A listed property whose status is warning makes proven false, as a violation would; its own status stays warning, and the verdict's blockedWarnings field names it. An id that names no property of this verdict is refused (ok false, errorKind invalid-arguments). Left out, warnings do not block.

tools.name: api_deploy
tools.description: If api_verify is proven under the declared topology, generate the Yichus API engine JavaScript (handlers + Principal injection + DB IO). Refuses when any property is violated or blocked, and when a property named in require is not proven. The emitted HTTP server refuses to listen unless YICHUS_AUTH is jwt (JWKS), clerk-api-key (API keys checked with Clerk via CLERK_SECRET_KEY), proxy-header (X-User-Id plus YICHUS_TRUST_PROXY_AUTH=1), or dev (YICHUS_DEV_AUTH=1). The engine also serves its routes as MCP tools at /mcp, so an agent can call the deployed API.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files for the API module.

port.description: Optional listen port for the generated engine (default 8080).

instances.description: Deployment topology: 1 for a single engine instance, many for multiple instances sharing one DB. Left out, the sources are verified as many but the engine still takes requests one at a time; pass many to run them side by side.

require.description: Optional JSON array of api_verify property ids (for example ["stored-field-disclosure"]) that must each be proven, not only free of violations: a warning or blocked status, or an id the verdict does not have, refuses the deploy.

tools.name: api_compile
tools.description: Parse and type-check Bosatsu API sources in memory (CompileKernel). No filesystem.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files.

tools.name: api_audit
tools.description: Audit IO composition from typed IR: read-then-write, orphaned IO, and writes without reads. These are diagnostics to interpret in context, not an application-wide safety proof. Use api_verify for the composite API gate.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files.

tools.name: api_permissions
tools.description: Compare declared Yichus/Service route permissions to inferred CRUD from handler effects. A missing or mismatched permission is separate from row access and caller authentication: api_access_check checks resource policies; the server engine enforces route identity and roles.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files.

tools.name: api_access_check
tools.description: Check resource policies from typed IR: OwnerScoped keys must derive from the runtime Principal; Guarded operations and row uses must follow supported declared guards; GuardedOrRoles also permits access when every route reaching the operation requires every listed role. An empty guards list is role-only. PublicReadRoleWrite permits reads and queries on any route but requires every listed route role for mutations, including ID allocation. Public imposes no owner-key or guard discipline. Reports holds/violated/inconclusive. Also returns routes, every declared route with discloses: each stored field path (table.field[].field) its response may carry, kind copied, computed, guard (it only decides which reply is sent) or released, via the release for released, precise false for a possible reach. An empty discloses list means the complete walk found no stored field; discloses is null, with disclosesBlocked reasons, when the walk cannot establish it. disclosesImprecise lists why any precise-false entry is only possible (empty when every entry is precise; null when blocked). Guard use does not prove that the guard expresses the intended business rule, and route authority relies on the server enforcing authenticated identities and roles.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files.

tools.name: api_integrity_check
tools.description: Complete typed causal order existence plus bounded per-cell race, stale-read, and declared Yichus/Spec checks. Inspect the returned claims: top-level ok and WebMCP isError describe tool execution, not whether properties hold. Default schema=legacy-2.2 retains verdicts.invariants; opt in to schema=3.0 for spec-verdict claims with typed subject, operation scope, completion and trust gaps. A declared model hold does not prove its implementation, and a sampled hold is inconclusive in 3.0. Truncated cells without a counterexample remain inconclusive; causal consistency alone does not certify model quality or database executions. TLC is not run; both schema views carry only a diagnostic sketch. For legacy-2.2, view=compact replaces only the inline sketch. For 3.0, it also deduplicates operations into an operationCatalog and uses numeric references in scopes and causal pairs. Both compact views carry a sketch hash and full-view retrieval request; view and schema are independent selectors.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files.

module_name.description: Optional module name for the verdict (default Api).

max_ops.description: Optional schedule bound (default 8, hard cap 8); does not limit complete causal graph checking.

view.description: Optional full (default) or compact. Compact retains the decision evidence and a retrieval reference for the diagnostic sketch. Unknown values are errors.

schema.description: Optional legacy-2.2 (default) or 3.0. Select the evidence schema independently of view; unknown values are errors.

tools.name: api_dist_check
tools.description: Run DistEngine on a declared Yichus/Dist DistSpec (multi-instance schedules, lost updates).

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files including the DistSpec.

max_schedules.description: Optional bound on explored schedules (default 20000); a world that needs more says so in its verdict.

depth.description: Optional bound on steps per schedule (default 12).

tools.name: api_escrow_check
tools.description: Run AdmissionSolver on a declared EscrowSpec (a State cell) or TableEscrowSpec (a table: one integer per row key, bounds read off another table's row). Pass batch JSON to admit/defer operations; a table spec is admitted against rows. Replay checks the admitted operations only. It does not establish that the handler rejects operations the declaration deferred, so it is not a general proof that the handler enforces the bounds.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files including the EscrowSpec or TableEscrowSpec.

batch.description: Optional JSON array of {operation, input, principal?} admission ops; principal is {user_id, roles} for a handler that takes one.

rows.description: Optional JSON world a TableEscrowSpec is admitted against: {table: [row, ...] | {id: row}}, the api_why rows form. An unseeded table is empty.

tools.name: api_report
tools.description: Build the program-report-2.0 map from the typed IR for whatever style of program the sources are (CRUD, flow, dist, escrow, unrouted IO). overview.surfaces names the present IR surfaces; needed names missing declarations with snippets. Pass format html for a self-contained HTML document.

protocol_case.description: Optional protocol-case-1.0 JSON; attaches a separate bounded protocol verdict without changing universal proof claims.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files for the module.

instances.description: Deployment topology: 1 for a single engine instance, many (default) for multiple instances sharing one DB.

format.description: json (default) for the raw report, html for a self-contained HTML document.

title.description: Optional title for the HTML document.

detail.description: summary (default) keeps shape to per-package counts plus the IO/notable bindings; full enumerates every binding.

tools.name: api_frontend
tools.description: If api_verify is proven, generate a self-contained HTML frontend from a Yichus/Frontend::FrontendSpec in the sources. Refuses unknown routes, unrepresentable handler extras, and unproven APIs. Transport (in-process or http) and auth (dev, clerk, auth0, api-key, bearer) are tool args.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files including the API module and the FrontendSpec.

instances.description: Deployment topology: 1 for a single engine instance, many for multiple instances sharing one DB. Left out, the sources are verified as many but an in-process engine still takes requests one at a time; pass many to run its requests side by side. With transport: http no engine is embedded: the sources are still verified under this topology, and the remote engine's own api_deploy decides how it takes requests.

transport.description: in-process (default; embed the engine) or http (fetch to api_base_url).

api_base_url.description: Required when transport is http: origin the generated app will POST to.

auth.description: dev (default; user-id field), clerk (a session token for a YICHUS_AUTH=jwt engine with Clerk's JWKS; a clerk-api-key engine answers it 401), auth0, api-key (http only, for a YICHUS_AUTH=clerk-api-key engine: the person pastes an API key the page sends as its Bearer credential and holds in memory only; the page never creates keys, Clerk issues them; a key carries no roles, so the API must declare no role_route), or bearer (in-process only: the app hands the engine a Bearer token it verifies itself against jwks; the page's test issuer or any RS256 issuer). Provider modes obtain a Bearer token only.

clerk_publishable_key.description: Clerk publishable key. Required when auth is clerk.

auth0_domain.description: Auth0 domain. Required when auth is auth0.

auth0_client_id.description: Auth0 SPA client id. Required when auth is auth0.

jwks.description: JWKS JSON (a {keys:[...]} object, as a string) the in-process engine verifies RS256 Bearer tokens against. Required when auth is bearer.

issuer.description: Optional expected iss claim for bearer auth.

audience.description: Optional expected aud claim for bearer auth.

roles_claim.description: Optional exact JWT payload key containing an array of role strings. Required to exercise role_route through in-process bearer auth.

store.description: Storage the embedded engine attaches at boot: memory (default; forgets on reload) or local:<name> (one localStorage key per table; survives reloads and a crash).

tools.name: api_add_artifact
tools.description: Return a paste-ready Bosatsu snippet for a report artifact (AccessSpec, ServiceDef, DistSpec, EscrowSpec, FlowSpec, Spec, FrontendSpec). Pass kind. Pass the same sources as api_report to fill names from the IR, or omit sources for a generic template. If the kind does not apply to those sources, the tool says so instead of emitting a misleading snippet.

kind.description: access, service, dist, escrow, flow, spec, or frontend

sources.description: Optional JSON array of {fileName, source}. When present, the snippet is filled from the typed IR.

resource.description: Optional table or cell name for generic access/escrow/spec templates.

policy.description: owner or public. Used for generic access templates.

name.description: Optional binding/service name for generic templates.

tools.name: api_law_check
tools.description: Check declared Yichus/Law obligations. Mode sampled (default) uses seeded generation: holds is bounded observation, never proof. Mode exhaustive checks every value of an accepted finite type or every distinct value of a Bosatsu FiniteObligation list; holds-exhaustive applies only to that recorded scope. Unsupported domains, exceeded limits, unfinished witnesses, and worker failures never become a pass. Violated and inconclusive both mean not done.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files including the Obligation bindings.

module_name.description: Optional module name for the verdict artifact (default Laws).

seed.description: Optional run seed; the whole run replays from this one number (default 41).

mode.description: sampled (default) or exhaustive; exhaustive never falls back to a seeded pass.

maximum.description: Maximum finite inputs per obligation in exhaustive mode (default 256, hard cap 4096).

tools.name: api_lean_check
tools.description: Ask a configured host (native, Node Wasm, or the isolated browser Lean Wasm page) to compile exact Bosatsu sources and run pinned Lean on supported Yichus/Law obligations. Pass sources to check, or receipt_sha256 alone to fetch the exact full receipt cached by this host. The compact view is the default agent result; view full returns the complete validated run. Its fullReceiptSha256 names exact full receipt bytes, not a portable proof: recompile and recheck across builds. The translator requires a direct Law.check and exactly one direct filled Witness. All three hosts support capture-free nonrecursive unary Bool predicates and a narrow structural List[Bool] predicate with self-calls only on the bound tail of a Nil/Cons match. The native host also supports a checked Int/product grammar with exported literal lean_proof and lean_witness scripts and the optional pinned Mathlib bundle. Lean checks generated recursion termination; author proof terms can cite existing Mathlib theorems. Mathlib is unavailable in the Node/browser Wasm runtime. Verified means generated law and witness theorems passed Lean elaboration and axiom audit over the recorded input type. Native receipts also record independent leanchecker replay; Wasm receipts explicitly set independentKernelReplay false. Compare method, scope, and completion before describing the proof. FiniteObligation is not admitted. A compact not-admitted row means this method could not check the law: withhold proof-dependent changes and seek another proof route. A not-verified row means Lean did not establish proof; inspect the full receipt. Unsupported laws, missing tools, timeouts, and empty obligation sets are inconclusive. The isolated browser Lean page supports the Wasm route through WebMCP; the general browser workbench reports unsupported-host guidance. Worked sources: https://yich.us/reference/api-mcp/examples.html#lean-bool and https://yich.us/reference/api-mcp/examples.html#lean-list and https://yich.us/reference/api-mcp/examples.html#lean-mathlib.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files including exported Obligation bindings; required unless fetching receipt_sha256.

receipt_sha256.description: Fetch the exact full receipt from this live host by the compact view's fullReceiptSha256; omit sources.

view.description: compact (default) or full; receipt retrieval always returns full.

tools.name: api_protocol_check
tools.description: Exhaustively explore a protocol-case-1.0 finite domain against compiled transaction handlers. Requests carry instance and delivery identities; serializable transactions are atomic; commit-unknown branches into committed and uncommitted durable states; external dispatch and response are separate transitions. Declare IO[Bool] invariants over immutable before/after views, required reachability witnesses, typed named inputs, times, external results, and budgets. Holds means only the complete declared finite domain; violated includes a sourced schedule; exhausted budgets and unsupported semantics are inconclusive. Adapter conformance, authenticated principals and absence of unlisted writers remain explicit assumptions. Use the same case with yichus protocol --case case.json files.bosatsu. Case schema, selector vocabulary and a runnable example: https://yich.us/reference/api-mcp/analysis-recipes.html#protocol and the full specification at https://yich.us/reference/api-mcp/protocol-specification.txt.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu handlers and declared invariant functions.

case.description: JSON object or encoded JSON string in protocol-case-1.0 format; all domains, assumptions, invariants and bounds are explicit.

tools.name: api_conformance_check
tools.description: Check declared Yichus/Spec Conformance and WorldConformance bindings by execution: the compiled handler runs in a real seeded world over generated inputs (one table for Conformance; every table, as one of the declared callers, for WorldConformance), and the declared step is compared against the projected world after every operation. Three-valued verdicts (holds is bounded observation, never proof); divergences render through the declaration's own describe and show_input, and name the caller in the world form. Violated and inconclusive both mean not done.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files including the Conformance or WorldConformance bindings.

module_name.description: Optional module name for the verdict artifact (default Conformance).

seed.description: Optional run seed; the whole run replays from this one number (default 41).

tools.name: api_obligations
tools.description: The guided commit-strategy surface: which strategy your discharged obligations license (serialized commit, per-key independence, single-write commit, lattice single-write, bounded witness search), and — when a faster one is one obligation away — one pre-written sentence saying what would make this faster plus one paste-ready law snippet. Discharge is fail-closed on verdict status: only laws with a holds verdict count, and holds is bounded evidence, never proof. The engine does not check that a named law expresses its obligation or that it applies to the deployed handler — those bindings are your assertions, restated in the verdict's unverifiedAssertions field — and the licensed strategy stays advisory until a later phase verifies them.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files including the laws and the Obligations binding.

seed.description: Optional run seed; the whole run replays from this one number (default 41).

tools.name: api_abstraction_map
tools.description: Draw the program's abstraction ladder: every definition placed at its abstraction height (layer 0 = built only from builtins; each layer composes the ones below), with reuse (fan-in), width (direct dependencies), mass (size: node count of the compiled definition), duplication (shape-isomorphic blocks repeated inside a definition, each listed in repeatedBlocks with every instance's source location, and copy-paste clone pairs across definitions), higher-order generators, curried specializations, and semantic policy objects (abstractionStructure), and layer-skipping edges measured. Optional peer_sources and peer_side attach the computed before/after organization diff (peerDiff), and optional peer_style (board, wires, strata, matrix, or brief) renders a side-by-side before/after SVG diagram at peerDiff.svg. Every visual quantity is a defined function of the source's dependency graph and the layout is deterministic, so you can inspect reuse and layer crossings. The layout does not score organization or establish that one graph shape is best. On the browser MCP page this tool also renders the map for the user, so sending sources here changes what they see.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files for the module.

peer_sources.description: Optional JSON array of {fileName, source} for a peer version (before or after) so the response includes peerDiff.

peer_side.description: With peer_sources: whether peer_sources is before or after (default after, so sources is the opposite side).

peer_style.description: With peer_sources: optional visual style for a standalone before/after SVG diagram at peerDiff.svg — board (3-tier whiteboard: entry points on top, shared rules in the middle with helpers folded in, domain data at the bottom; suits explaining a refactor to a teammate), wires (layered call graph; suits tracing direct call arrows and skip-layer lanes), strata (stacked layer shelves without crossing wires; suits comparing layer height and reuse), matrix (caller-by-callee grid; suits auditing dense call tables), or brief (compact change cards; suits a pull request summary).

tools.name: api_organize
tools.description: Render one organization lens over the module as the text the CLI's `organize` prints: page (how organized the program is, at a glance: layers, blocks, holes), vocabulary (the declared concepts, their operations by role, embedded concepts, unreferenced concepts, and bare-scalar parameters), stack (the blocks by layer in the order a reader learns them, with reuse), conventions (how the project writes each recurring shape and where it disagrees with itself), aid (the separate heuristic reading for a weaker reader; clearly labeled as such), map (the definitions by layer with compiled size, reuse, direct dependencies, duplicated mass, and layer-skipping branches), abstractions (higher-order generators and parameter slots, curried partial applications, call-site instantiations with semantic policy objects or passed functions, the security/effect responsibility split across routes, and declared Yichus/Organize::AbstractionSpec claims with GuardResponsibility InGenerator, ByPolicyObject(concept), InPassedFunction, EnvelopeOnly, or NoGuardClaim checked deterministically against the IR; when you extract a rule that several definitions now call, declare it with AbstractionSpec(name, generator, NoGuardClaim, [members]) so the check can confirm every member reaches it on every path; `abstractions` in the result holds generators, specializations, instantiations, routeShapes, and declaredAbstractions), flow (the effect sequences in causal order under declared backing systems and expectations), layers (the packages in rows by level, the packages each one uses with how many of their definitions, and the direct effect sites and tables in each package's own definitions; `layers` in the result holds the packages with their definitions and levels, and the package and definition edges, all from type-checked references), structure (pictures drawn from where values go and from the checked types: records of functions and the values that fill them, whether each call through a record or a handed-in function gets it from a parameter or reaches for it by name, values built step by step, packages as phases by the types they make and take, and what each caller does with a shared definition's result: returns it as is on every path or on some paths, works on it further, only branches on it, runs it for its effect and keeps no value, or drops it; a record or effect handle is handed in on every path, reached for or built here on every path, or handed in on some paths only or not traced; when requirements is passed, `scenarios` in the result holds one decision tree per entry, computed by following values from the handler into the definitions it calls: nodes are branch points whose test comes from the request, the caller, a handle read or a call result, with the declared authority and roles first, arms carry their pattern, leaves carry the outcome and every effect on the path, and arms that change neither are folded), effects (each declared route as a tree, in source order, of every effect its handler can reach: the calls to it, the IO values handed to a definition as an argument, the typed branch tests around it, and transaction scopes; `effects` in the result holds one row per effect use with its route, table, site, the chain of definitions with the frames around each position, passedTo and under) or writes (the same with only row writes). The effects lens states structure; it does not judge whether a write should sit under a wrapper or a guard. With a view argument over stack, map, or conventions, an authored view (order, foreground, declared groups, captions) renders under the unchanged page or is refused with the reason. The implementations lens returns a structured comparison: all typed user references, signatures, direct primitive effects, access findings, and located compiled repetition. Its nested groups and role meanings are authored, never inferred architecture or permission proof. The composition lens returns source-composition-1 under composition plus a text diagram. It joins checked source occurrences, escrow declaration roles and operation targets, verified flow matches and named parts, and static effect-use contexts. All supplied user definitions remain visible, including disconnected declarations; unresolved evidence and scope are explicit. Source references, declared targets and matched bodies have different meanings. It accepts optional exact qualified focus for effect expansion, and takes no authored view. For a large program, pass read to obtain a bounded source-composition-read-1 page: package inventory, package definitions, a definitions search, resolved direct user-binding relationships, then an exact occurrence witness. Definitions search requires nonempty where with exact package, opaque checked signatureId, exported, usedOutside, and/or referencesBinding filters; all predicates combine with AND and results sort by qualified ID. Missing identities fail; direct references do not establish execution. Each page reports snapshot, scope and continuation; binding reads include incoming and outgoing counts. Effects and unresolved evidence require a separate complete composition request. The existing complete composition response and exact focus remain available when read is omitted. The page lists; the reader judges.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files for the module.

lens.description: page, vocabulary, stack, conventions, aid, map, abstractions, flow, layers, structure, effects, writes, composition (source relationships and declaration parts), or implementations (structured nested map and comparison).

title.description: Optional title line (default: the first file name).

view.description: For implementations, required JSON string: {schemaVersion: "implementation-view-1", question, pins: [qualified binding ids], groups: [{id, label, parent?: group id, members: [qualified binding ids]}], roles: [{id, label, references: [qualified binding ids]}]}. Optional order lists group:<id> or node:<qualified binding> layout identities to override automatic peer ordering; dependency bands are retained. Each binding has at most one direct group; parents must be acyclic. Cells are keyed by pin id then role id. Unknown identities or fields are rejected. Otherwise, optional VIEW document over stack, map, or conventions: {lens, order, foreground, groups, captions}. The page renders unchanged and the view renders under it: the author's order and foreground, groups that must be families the program declares (Yichus/Organize::FamilySpec), captions of at most 160 characters with no verdict word, labeled says:. A view naming an unknown id, an undeclared group, a verdict word, or leaving out a mandatory fact (the stack's roots; a declared family's divergent members) is refused: text carries the page alone and viewRefused names the element and the reason.

focus.description: For composition: exact Package/Name::binding effect root, retaining the complete user-definition graph. For map: a definition name to zoom in on with radius 2. For stack: a block's bare name (when unique) or Pkg/Name::binding; the svg then draws that block and every block it is built from, transitively, under the same rules, and its legend counts the blocks and edges outside that cone, while the text page is unchanged. An unknown or ambiguous name is refused with the candidates. Bounding the focus to N steps and drawing one box per package are CLI only: yichus organize stack --svg --focus NAME --depth N FILES, or yichus organize stack --svg --packages FILES.

read.description: For composition only: optional JSON object selecting a bounded read. Use {scope: "packages"}, then {scope: "package", id: "Pkg/Name"}, then {scope: "definitions", where: {package: "Pkg/Name", exported: true}}, then {scope: "binding", id: "Pkg/Name::binding"}, and {scope: "witness", id: "relation occurrence id"}. The definitions where object requires at least one exact filter: package, opaque checked signatureId, exported, usedOutside, or referencesBinding (qualified direct target); predicates combine with AND and rows sort by qualified ID. Optional limit and cursor page the selected facts; expectedSnapshot refuses stale source. The response returns snapshot, exact scope and continuation; binding reads include incoming and outgoing counts. It does not expand effects or unresolved evidence: use a separate complete composition request for the latter and a focused request for effect contexts. Omit read for the complete diagram.

requirements.description: For structure only: optional JSON object, the author's requirements document; its scenarios array [{entry, title, names: {computed id: words}, expect: [{at: computed id, claim}]}] is checked against the computed scenario trees and returned as claims. A claim is [not] reads TABLE, writes TABLE, refused, returns CONSTRUCTOR, reaches model or reaches net; any other text is reported as not-a-claim. An unknown entry is a mismatch and a name or at for an id the engine did not compute is refused.

tools.name: api_composition_diff
tools.description: Compare two complete Bosatsu source sets through the shared source-composition-diff reader (source-composition-diff-read-4). Start with an overview read: its first page carries a compact gist (added, removed and changed packages, added/removed/changed definitions with signatures before and after where they changed, new and removed cross-package references, definitions that started or stopped referencing themselves, packages that gained or lost an imported package or import item and those whose declared import set is unchanged, declared service routes added, removed or changed by service and path with their handler, required roles, table permissions and rate limits, channel limits) and states every supplied package added, removed, changed or unchanged with its import changes when it fits the response cap; an oversized overview explicitly marks its summary partial and offers a snapshot-bound {scope: "packages"} cursor for every package row. A reference that only moved within its body is one moved event. Then open a returned exact event id with a witness read. Both sides compile through the Yichus kernel. Every result retains before and after snapshots, channel availability, and bounded changes. This structure-only path currently reports the effect channel unavailable; it does not silently equate absent effect events with unchanged effects. A package supplied on only one side is reported added or removed relative to the supplied source sets, with its definitions, imports and relations as events; the tool cannot know about files the caller did not supply. A source set that fails compilation fails the call; it is never read as removed definitions. Checked variant type events retain constructor order and field signatures, and variant-use events compare grouped checked counts by exact type, constructor, owner, use kind and location precision. Variant type declarations in packages supplied on only one side are source-set additions or removals. When package sets differ, variant-use counts are partial over shared supplied owner packages or unavailable without overlap; an unmatched type does not become a false use removal. A composition diff describes checked source structure, not behavioral equivalence or whether a proposed change is desirable. The same request works with yichus organize composition-diff --read request.json --before ... --after ... and browser WebMCP.

before_sources.description: Complete BEFORE Bosatsu source set as a JSON array of {fileName, source}.

after_sources.description: Complete AFTER Bosatsu source set as a JSON array of {fileName, source}.

read.description: Required bounded request: {scope: "overview", limit?: 1..64, cursor?, expectedBefore?, expectedAfter?} (gist and packages on the first page when they fit; otherwise explicit partial summary and package cursor), {scope: "packages", limit?: 1..64, cursor?, expectedBefore?, expectedAfter?} for complete package rows, or {scope: "witness", id: exact event id, expectedBefore?, expectedAfter?}. Cursors bind the snapshot pair; mismatches fail.

tools.name: api_world_shape
tools.description: Describe the in-memory world api_why and api_conformance_check run IO handlers in: per table, the row type, whether the row under an id is one record or the whole list, the record's fields, the id rule, the principal's JSON form and the enum form. Facts about the declared types, never about a run; read it before writing rows or inputs.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files for the module.

tools.name: api_why
tools.description: Evaluate ONE binding on concrete typed inputs and report why the output is what it is. Pick the binding from a diagram or report by its Pkg/Name::binding id. Provide inputs as JSON (missing ones are seeded deterministically); the tool returns the typed inputs and output with named rendering, soundFacts (static dataflow: per-parameter influence that holds for EVERY input), and observed (bounded seeded runs: touched bindings, per-parameter and per-field vary-one-fix-rest differentials). soundFacts and observed are disjoint on purpose: an observed-constant result is NOT independence, and every observed sentence says 'bounded observation, not proof'. IO handlers run against a fresh in-memory world (optionally seeded via rows) and report the table rows after the run; handler differentials rebuild the world from the same seeded rows for every variation (a varied principal's roles against fixed rows flips a gated route).

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files for the module.

binding.description: The binding to evaluate, as Pkg/Name::binding (the id shown on diagrams and reports).

inputs.description: Optional JSON object {param: value} of provided inputs. Values use the same JSON encoding api types use; a nullary enum constructor is written {"Ctor": {}} (the form the tool prints), and the bare object of a constructor's fields is read too. Unlisted params are seeded from the seed.

seed.description: Optional run seed; the whole run replays byte-identically from this one number (default 41).

observe.description: Optional; false skips the differential runs and returns only the evaluation plus soundFacts (default true).

rows.description: Optional JSON object {table: [row, ...]} seeding the in-memory world for an IO handler run.

tools.name: api_suggest_properties
tools.description: Propose Yichus/Law obligations from the program's reified facts. Each suggestion is a complete standalone Bosatsu file whose unfillable pieces are named holes; paste it beside your module, or decline it with a Dismissed binding. Runs the default rules plus any RuleSet declared in the sources.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files for the module.

module_name.description: Optional module name for the suggestions artifact (default Laws).

tools.name: api_report_brief
tools.description: Package the report's derived facts (headline, map, guarantees, needed, facts) with constant writing instructions, ready to hand to any LLM that should produce an orientation narrative. The output is fully deterministic: the engine prepares the data and names the task; the prose is the consumer's. Use api_report for the full artifact.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files for the module.

instances.description: Deployment topology: 1 for a single engine instance, many (default) for multiple instances sharing one DB.

tools.name: api_glance
tools.description: Compare several programs side by side on one scale: vocabulary share, abstraction layers and mass, duplication and clone groups, declared mutation flows. Every channel shares one scale across the programs, rows are in name order, and the rendering is deterministic ASCII. Each program is compiled separately with builtin shadowing, so a program that declares a Yichus/* package is read as its own version of it. Use api_organize with the map lens for one program in depth; this is the across-programs view. Same job as yichus glance --program name=files.

programs.description: JSON array of {name, sources} where sources is the usual array of {fileName, source}. At least one; each is compiled on its own.

title.description: Optional title for the comparison header (default: the program names).

tools.name: api_properties
tools.description: The per-binding property digest: for every binding the input files declare, the structural facts the explorer and claim checking read. Pure -- a function of the loaded program, with no clock and no randomness -- and restricted to the packages the input files declare, so builtins do not appear. Same job as yichus properties.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files. The digest is restricted to the packages these files declare, matched by fileName.

tools.name: api_yir
tools.description: Export the canonical YIR (Yichus IR) of a program: the versioned artifact other tooling reads, with its schema version, packages and binding count. Well-formedness is a refusal, not a warning -- an ill-formed export is never returned, because the point of the artifact is that its shape can be trusted. Same job as yichus yir, which writes it to a file; this returns it.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files to export.

tools.name: api_verify_claims
tools.description: Check an agent's claims about a program against the program's own facts. Each claim gets a three-valued verdict with the evidence that decided it; absence claims are backed by the agenda's enumeration, so "zero cards in scope" carries the examined count as its evidence. A refuted claim is a successful check that found something -- the call stays ok and the refuted field says so. Use this before reporting a finding, not after. Same job as yichus verify-claims, which reads the claims from a file and turns refutals into a nonzero exit code.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files the claims are about.

claims.description: JSON object (or encoded JSON string) with a claims array, each claim naming what it asserts about the program.

entries.description: Optional JSON array of the program's entry package names, e.g. ["Demo/App"], the unused-export premise as in api_explore's agenda: declared, unused-export cards are drawn and claims about them are decided; absent, they are not drawn and such a claim is not-provable. A name that is not a supplied package fails the call.

tools.name: api_dossier
tools.description: The one-shot trace dossier: every binding with its source location, snippet, inferred type, effect class and dependencies. With a focus binding, the dossier narrows to that binding's transitive dependency closure, focus first and breadth-first after -- one call instead of a walk. A focus that names no binding, or an ambiguous bare name, is an error listing the candidates, never a silent whole-program dossier. Same job as yichus dossier, which writes the file; this returns it.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files.

binding.description: Optional focus: a bare binding name (must be unambiguous) or Pkg/Path/name to pin the package. Omitted, the dossier covers every binding.

tools.name: api_fact_diff
tools.description: Diff the fact families between two versions of a program: which agenda cards appeared, vanished or changed, so a review reads the DELTA a change made rather than re-reading the whole program. Optional delta claims are checked against the same report and answered with refuted, exactly as api_verify_claims answers claims about one version. Same job as yichus fact-diff, which reads the two versions from disk and turns refutals into a nonzero exit code.

before_sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} for the BEFORE version.

after_sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} for the AFTER version.

claims.description: Optional JSON object with a claims array, each claim naming a subject and the change it asserts.

entries.description: Optional JSON array of the program's entry package names, e.g. ["Demo/App"], the unused-export premise as in api_explore's agenda, applied to both versions: declared, unused-export cards are drawn and diffed; absent, they are not drawn and a delta claim about them is not-provable. A name either version does not supply fails the call, naming that version.

tools.name: api_diff
tools.description: Structurally diff two versions of a program binding by binding, from the typed IR rather than the text: what changed inside each binding and where. With verdict, returns the PR-diff dossier instead of the raw report. Both versions are Bosatsu sources, not serialized profiles. Same job as yichus diff.

before_sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} for the BEFORE version.

after_sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} for the AFTER version.

verdict.description: Emit the PR-diff dossier verdict (artifact contract) instead of the raw structural report.

tools.name: api_workbook
tools.description: Orient in a program, inspect binding contracts, or find what a proposed change can affect. Returns the same JSON artifacts as yichus workbook: package mode includes package summaries, a binding catalog and per-binding detail; impact mode follows reverse dependencies from a required binding; dossier mode follows the focus binding's dependencies. Omit binding in package or dossier mode for the whole program. Unknown or ambiguous focus names fail with candidates instead of silently broadening the answer.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files.

binding.description: Focus: an unambiguous bare name or Pkg/Path/name. Required for impact mode.

catalog_only.description: In package mode, omit per-binding detail while keeping package summaries and the catalog (default false). Ignored in other modes, as in the CLI.

tools.name: api_explore
tools.description: Inspect a program's typed structure. Start with overview for effects, dataflow, structural signals and boundaries. Agenda enumerates located facts with coverage counts (page with nextCursor until absent); it also runs pure bindings on seeded inputs and labels those results as bounded observations, not proofs. Use explore to navigate paths, search to find structural matches, connections for immediate edges, trace for dependencies, trace_flow for provenance edges, and path for a route between bindings. Each verb delegates to the same SystemProfileApi engine as yichus explore. Returns response with the explorer's type and payload. Paths accept Pkg/Path/binding or default/Pkg/Path/binding; root is empty. Only the parameters documented for the selected verb are accepted. Daemon process management and user-authored query programs are not included.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files.

verb.description: Required: explore, connections, search, trace, trace_flow, overview, agenda or path.

path.description: explore/overview: optional path, defaults to root. connections: required nonempty path.

direction.description: connections only: both (default), incoming or outgoing.

kind.description: connections only: optional exact edge-kind filter from a previous response.

query.description: search only, required: structural query, e.g. kind:binding. Same query syntax as yichus explore --search.

scope.description: search only: optional path restricting the search.

binding.description: trace/trace_flow only, required: binding path to start from.

monad.description: trace/trace_flow only: effect type, default Yichus/IO::IO.

overlay.description: overview only: all (default), effects, dataflow, signals or boundaries.

limit.description: overview: maximum per section (default 6). agenda: page size (default 1). Integer >= 1.

card_type.description: agenda only: optional card type such as dead-field, discarded-argument or literal-result; unknown types fail with the full list.

cursor.description: agenda only: integer >= 0 (default 0), then use response.result.nextCursor.

package.description: agenda only: optional exact package filter; coverage counts remain program-wide.

entries.description: agenda only: JSON array of the program's entry package names, e.g. ["Demo/App"]. unused-export cards are drawn only when entries are declared: their exports, and every name a package they reach imports, are used; without entries the unused-export coverage row says notChecked. A name that is not a supplied package fails the call.

from.description: path only, required: starting binding path.

to.description: path only, required: destination binding path.

tools.name: api_flow
tools.description: Check whether declared mutations follow their FlowSpec factory before shipping a family of similar handlers. report returns extracted named parts and located divergences; failed means a divergence or declaration error (the CLI exits 1). batch replays operations all-or-nothing in memory, never against a live store; admitted=false is a rejected batch, not a tool error. equivalence compares extracted composition with each mutation on seeded inputs: bounded observation, not proof; not-provable stays explicit and only refuted sets failed, as on the CLI. parts refuses any divergent mutation and returns Bosatsu source only after compiling it. Same engine and selection policy as yichus flow: batch and parts require exactly one selected flow; with no flow name any broken declaration fails selection, with a name unrelated broken declarations are returned as warnings.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source}, including program and FlowSpec declarations.

mode.description: report (default, every declaration), batch, equivalence, or parts.

flow.description: Declared flow name for batch, equivalence or parts; report always covers every declaration.

batch.description: For batch mode, JSON object (or encoded JSON) with operations: [{mutation: Pkg/Name/binding, input: ...}]. Pass exactly one of batch or ops.

ops.description: For batch mode, a typed List[FlowOp[i, r]] binding as Pkg/Name/binding, instead of batch JSON.

package_name.description: For parts mode, emitted package name (default the spec package followed by /Parts).

runs.description: Positive number of equivalence inputs per mutation (default 5); zero or negative runs are rejected.

tools.name: api_composition_proposal
tools.description: Record authored structural changes against an exact checked source-composition snapshot. The proposal JSON must carry composition-proposal-1 or -2, baselineSnapshot, nonempty intent and 1-128 add/remove definition or relation operations; -2 also accepts add-export/remove-export {binding} and add-import/remove-import {package, binding}, where package is the importing package and binding the qualified imported definition. The composition-proposal-read-2 overview assesses declarations from the baseline's typed exports and imports: each cross-package source-reference relation, removed definition and import left unused names its required export/import edits as present, authored or missing, and any package import cycle. An added relation that already exists is already-present with its baseline relation IDs. The overview's impact lists, for each existing definition whose outgoing relations change, its direct and transitive baseline consumers; page them with {scope: impact}. This tool recompiles all sources and rejects stale snapshots, unknown identities, duplicate definition targets, relation removals or declaration edits, and inconsistent operations. Repeated added relations can represent distinct future occurrences. The bounded proposal page is an authored plan, never checked source or a behavior proof. Optional after_sources compiles a second full program and returns both structural observations and a bounded actual diff that exposes unexpected changes. Observations are relative to the supplied source sets: a package in only one of sources and after_sources is observed as added or removed, so its definitions appear as observed removals or unplanned changes; an unavailable channel leaves its steps inconclusive. No result proves behavioral equivalence or architectural quality. Use api_organize composition read to obtain the baseline snapshot and checked relation IDs before proposing removals.

sources.description: Complete baseline [{fileName, source}] Bosatsu source set; compiled to check baselineSnapshot.

proposal.description: Authored composition-proposal-1 or composition-proposal-2 JSON object with baselineSnapshot, intent and operations; a JSON-encoded string is also accepted.

read.description: Optional bounded {scope: overview, limit?, cursor?, expectedBaseline?}, {scope: impact, limit?, cursor?, expectedBaseline?} or {scope: witness, id, expectedBaseline?}; defaults to overview. Cursors are bound to the proposal and scope.

after_sources.description: Optional complete second [{fileName, source}] Bosatsu source set for structural observation only. Supply every package: a package on only one side is observed as added or removed, not skipped.

diff_read.description: With after_sources: optional bounded actual composition diff overview, packages, or exact witness request. Defaults to overview, so unexpected changes remain visible.
